item.description: The move buys good will with President Trump while costing the President Vladimir V. Putin — who is wanted for war crimes — little.

item.title: Trump Approval Hits New Low Two Weeks Before Midterms, Poll Finds
item.description: Likely voters favored Democratic candidates over Republicans by 11 percentage points in their congressional district, a New York Times/Siena poll found.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer and Ruth Igielnik

item.title: Christianity Today, a Voice of Centrist Evangelicalism, Is in Turmoil
item.description: Former employees of the publication say new leadership has been pushing back on independent journalism. About half of its staff members have left or been laid off over 14 months.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Graham
item.media:credit: Justin Merriman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bonnie Kristian, Christianity Today’s deputy editor until recently, said the outlet displays “an increasingly muddled sense of its place within American evangelicalism.”

item.title: How a Democrat Positioned Himself to Be Alaska’s Next Governor
item.description: As a mountaineer and extreme runner, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is thoroughly Alaskan, and thanks to Republican infighting and the state’s deep troubles, he just might win next month.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:description: “I want to get back to the Alaska that I grew up with and loved,” said Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democrat who may well become the state’s next governor.

item.title: In San Francisco, a Family Earning $325,000 Qualifies for Government Aid
item.description: With the A.I. boom driving up prices, the city is subsidizing child care for households with high incomes. Even with the help, families say they are struggling.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight
item.media:credit: Christie Hemm Klok for The New York Times
item.media:description: Natsumi Makiyama and John Marman, a married couple in San Francisco, together make just under $235,000, qualifying them for free child care under a city program.

item.title: New Video Shows Chaotic Moments Before Police Shot 1-Year-Old Kohen Wiley
item.description: The body-camera and surveillance footage provides the first glimpse of a confrontation in a Walmart parking lot that left 1-year-old Kohen Wiley dead.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Cranney, Mukta Joshi, Eduardo Medina and Devon Lum
item.media:credit: Carlos Kosienski/Sipa USA, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The shooting death of Kohen Wiley, a toddler, at a Walmart set off weeks of protests and calls for transparency in Senatobia, Miss.

item.title: Trump Wields an Unprecedented $277 Million in Final Midterm Stretch
item.description: The enormous spending by the term-limited president’s super PAC has no parallel in American history, and could offer struggling Republican candidates a lifeline.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: Since returning to office, President Trump has raised hundreds of millions of dollars into his super PAC, MAGA Inc., including contributions from donors and corporations with business before his administration.

item.title: How Zelensky Is Trying to Navigate Trump’s Tilt Toward Russia
item.description: Peter Baker, our chief White House correspondent, reports from Oslo, where Ukraine’s President, Volodymyr Zelensky, met with President Trump’s special envoy, Steve Witkoff.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker, Joy Sung and Paul Abowd

item.title: Ahead of Midterms, Justice Kagan Says Rulings Have Intensified Polarization
item.description: The justice said during a discussion that recent Supreme Court decisions on voting rights, gerrymandering and campaign finance have deepened America’s divides.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:description: Justice Elena Kagan in Washington this summer. Justice Kagan, one of the court’s three liberals, has issued strongly worded dissents in individual election-related cases.

item.title: U.S. Begins Disclosing C.I.A. Interview Reports From Scrutiny of Post-9/11 Torture
item.description: The rolling release of long-secret files could add detail to the history of a legally disputed Bush-era counterterrorism program.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Savage
item.media:description: The C.I.A. headquarters in Langley, Va.

item.title: ICE Says It Didn’t Hit a Biker With a Car. Video Raises Questions.
item.description: Video footage shows the moment in Long Beach, Calif., when a vehicle swerves toward an oncoming cyclist. The mayor has called for an investigation into ICE agents’ treatment of the rider.
item.dc:creator: Madison Malone Kircher
item.media:credit: Obtained by The New York Times
item.media:description: The street in Long Beach, Calif., where ICE agents detained a man on Saturday.

item.title: How Two Colorado House Candidates Are Thinking About AI

item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:credit: Matthew Defeo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Manny Rutinel, left, and Representative Gabe Evans.

item.title: A Billionaire Wanted a Trump Pardon. His Family Gave Alina Habba a $50 Million Deal.
item.description: Julio Herrera Velutini, a prominent Venezuelan, was seeking clemency. He got it not long after his daughter gave Ms. Habba, a lawyer close to President Trump, an extraordinarily lucrative job.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager
item.media:description: Julio Herrera Velutini in San Juan, Puerto Rico, in August 2022, after being charged for his role in a scheme to bribe the territory’s governor, Wanda Vázquez, to dismiss a regulator who was investigating his bank.

item.title: MAGA Inc. Unleashes Millions to Turn Out Republicans At the Polls
item.description: MAGA Inc. is now flooding the social media platforms with targeted ads as it seeks to turn out Republicans amid the president’s historically low approval ratings.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mr. Trump’s super PAC, MAGA Inc., spent more than $1.1 million in online ads on Saturday alone.

item.title: Michigan Senate Candidates Make Dueling Pitches to Business Leaders in Detroit
item.description: Mike Rogers and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the candidates in the tight race, defended their economic policies at the Detroit Economic Club.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon

item.title: In Texas’ Senate Race, Paxton and Talarico Converge on Key Battleground
item.description: In Tarrant County, a fight over polling places has energized Democrats as Republicans seek to defend their grip on a longtime stronghold.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman and Jesus Jiménez

item.title: Mailers About Transgender Students Mysteriously Appear at Texas Homes
item.description: The messages purporting to offer help for transgender students are tied to a group set up last month in Wyoming.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McGaughy
item.media:credit: Shelby Tauber for The New York Times
item.media:description: Letters and text messages are being sent out to Texas voters regarding transgender children as early voting has begun statewide.

item.title: She Braved Sharks and Storms to Swim the Length of California
item.description: “It feels surreal being done, this has been my entire life for nearly four months,” said Catherine Breed, who finished her historic journey near the Mexico border on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nick Romeo and Gabriela Bhaskar

item.title: Trump Pushes to Evict White House Press Corps

item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan
item.media:credit: Andrew Leyden for The New York Times
item.media:description: The White House press corps has worked from the Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House since the Nixon administration.

item.title: Republican Women Hail Working-Mom Credentials to Boost Hinson in Iowa Senate Race
item.description: Senator Katie Britt of Alabama was the latest national Republican to visit Iowa to campaign for Representative Ashley Hinson. President Trump will follow on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: Senator Katie Britt, center, credited Ashley Hinson, the Iowa Senate candidate, with helping her adapt to raising children while in Congress.

item.title: Alabama Man’s Death Sentence Is Commuted as Governor Cites Thin Evidence
item.description: Toforest Johnson’s conviction in the 1995 killing of a sheriff’s deputy relied on the testimony of a woman who was paid a $5,000 reward by the state for providing information.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Medina
item.media:description: It is the third time that Gov. Kay Ivey, a Republican, has commuted the death sentence of a prisoner.

item.title: If Democrats Win Congress, Could the G.O.P. Refuse to Seat Them?
item.description: A changing of the congressional guard in January could leave room for meddling, though most legal scholars doubt it would happen.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: Some lawmakers and commentators have turned their attention to the possibility that Republicans in Congress could try to block Democrats from assuming the majority.

item.title: Flamingo Birdnapping in Las Vegas Ends With a Cruelty Conviction
item.description: The man, visiting from Canada, carried a flamingo named Peachy from its habitat to his hotel room. He was convicted of felony and misdemeanor charges.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather and Remy Tumin
item.media:credit: Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Las Vegas Review-Journal, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The man convicted in the case, Mitchell Fairbarn, left, in court with his lawyer, Josh Tomsheck.

item.title: Trump’s D.C. Golf Course Renovation Plan Has Many Residents Feeling Discouraged
item.description: At East Potomac Park, several residents bemoaned a plan to revamp the federal property that might wipe out features they have cherished for years.
item.dc:creator: Clarence Williams and Campbell Robertson
item.media:credit: Andrew Leyden for The New York Times
item.media:description: The plan to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links in Washington could eventually overtake areas like a miniature golf course, bike trail and picnic area.

item.title: Richard Riehle, Prolific Actor Who Appeared in ‘Office Space,’ Dies at 78
item.description: Mr. Riehle, best remembered for playing an anxious character with “people skills,” built a career in theater, TV and film that lasted more than half a century.
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan
item.media:description: Richard Riehle, seen at a premiere in Hollywood in 2011. His character’s workplace anxiety and reliance on “people skills” made him one of the most memorable characters in the film “Office Space.”

item.title: Ramaswamy Campaign Attack Ad Featuring Amy Acton’s Mother Turns Ohio Governor’s Race Uglier
item.description: A Republican ad features Amy Acton’s estranged mother calling her daughter a liar. The two have not spoken since Dr. Acton’s mother backed her husband after his arrest on rape charges.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Contrera

item.title: Michael Bloomberg Gives $80 Million to Help Democrats in Final Midterm Push
item.description: The money from the former New York City mayor and megadonor, who is focused on ensuring a sizable Democratic House majority, will help cut into Republicans’ financial advantage.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer and Benjamin Oreskes
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michael R. Bloomberg’s donations will make him one of the largest known left-leaning donors in the midterms.

item.title: Trump Invokes Antisemitic Trope Again at Rally for Kansas Senator
item.description: President Trump said that opponents of Senator Roger Marshall had unfairly cast him as “some kind of a Shylock-type guy.” Mr. Trump used the same slur last year at a rally in Iowa.
item.dc:creator: Evan Gorelick
